analysis:
The Prime Minister announced the Jal Jeevan Mission in his Independence Day address on 15 August 2019, with a stated goal of tap water to every rural household by 2024 and an outlay of more than Rs 3.5 lakh crore.

At launch, 3.23 crore (about 17%) of rural households had tap water connections. Government data show that as on 18 July 2026, about 15.89 crore of 19.36 crore rural households (82.09%) had a tap water connection.

The 100% coverage target for 2024 was not met; coverage continued to rise after 2024 and the mission has been extended. Government releases count reported connections, while functionality (regular, adequate supply) is a separate measure.
notes: Some official communications cite slightly different totals for the same period (e.g. 15.19 crore in October 2024, 15.72 crore later), reflecting updated state reporting.
